title: A1 Clients, empty account
notice: No Dashboard, no Work queue, no switcher. A sender with no clients never sees agency furniture.

title: A1 Clients, nothing assigned
notice: A different empty state from the one above: the account has clients, this person has none.

title: A2 Add Client, step 1
notice: Create or connect is the first question, because it changes everything after it.

title: A2 Add Client, connect path
notice: One step, not three. The agency funds nothing, so there are no limits to set.

section: Launch day, for an agency that already exists
title: M1 Migration summary
notice: Numbers, not reassurance. The totals reconcile, and only clients the migration actually converted are listed.

section: Launch day, for an agency that already exists
title: M1, clean migration
notice: Nothing to review and nothing flagged, so one button out instead of a decision.

section: Launch day, for an agency that already exists
title: M2 Prospect review
notice: A suggestion is shown but never pre-selected. Keep in agency is the default, because a wrong guess puts one client's lead in another client's workspace.

title: A0 Dashboard
notice: Health strip, then KPIs, then the clients table as the launchpad. Decisions in the right rail carry their controls in the row.

title: Q1 Work queue
notice: One list ordered by what it costs to ignore, not by item type. Every row carries its client.

title: A1 Client Management
notice: The default column set is measured to fit a 1440px laptop with no horizontal scroll.

title: A1, choosing columns
notice: The real table organism's column selector. Client Name is locked; Budget, Active Sequences and Total Prospects are one click away.

title: A2 Add Client, step 2 Access
notice: Who from the agency works on this client, and what the client's own people can do.

title: A2 Add Client, step 3 Limits
notice: Caps drawn against the pool, with what is unallocated shown per resource.

title: A3 Client record, Overview
notice: Setup checklist, outcomes, usage and the facts. The entry point to everything else about this client.

title: A4 Access
notice: Two kinds of member in one list: agency staff and the client's own people, with the invite state visible.

title: A5 Limits
notice: Cap and reservation per resource, with the pool consequence stated for each change.

title: A6 Email Accounts
notice: A mailbox belongs to exactly one workspace, which is why the migration flags shared ones rather than splitting them.

title: A7 Billing, Client allocation
notice: Hybrid as built: one shared pool, an independent budget per client on request, linked clients on their own plan. One of three models; Dhruv has not weighed in. Every pool is deliberately over-allocated. Caps may oversubscribe; reservations may not.

title: B1 Billing, Account plan usage
notice: One plan, bought once. A client has a limit against these pools, not a wallet.

title: Sequences, agency workspace
notice: The agency's own campaigns for winning clients. Client work is not rolled up here, which is the whole point of the note at the top.

title: CRM, agency workspace
notice: The agency's own prospects: companies it wants as clients. Cascade Partners appears because the agency prospected and won it.

title: Email Accounts, agency workspace
notice: A mailbox belongs to exactly one workspace, so a client's mailboxes cannot appear here without being unassigned there.

title: Analytics, agency workspace
notice: The agency's own numbers only. Portfolio performance across clients is the Dashboard, a different question.

title: Dialer, agency workspace
notice: A module this feature does not change, stated as scoped rather than faked. What matters is the scoping note.

title: Sequences, an agency with none of its own
notice: Many agencies only run client work. Empty here is a choice, not a fault, and the copy says so.

title: Unified Inbox, across your clients
notice: One of the two modules that does roll up. Safe for the same reason the queue is: filtered by assignment, and every row names its client.

title: Tasks, across your clients
notice: One task list, not three. Ordered as created; the cost-ordered version of the same work is the Work queue.

title: Unified Inbox, the agency's own
notice: The same module switched to the agency's own campaigns. No client rows at all in this scope.

title: The master workspace
notice: Administration only, decided 11 Sep. Dashboard, Work queue, Client Management, the two cross-client roll-ups, the estate, the shared library, Billing. No outreach of its own.

title: The agency's own outreach workspace
notice: Peer to a client workspace, in the same switcher, and capped on the same pool. Campaigns to win clients never mix with client work in either direction.

title: The switcher, one click from any screen
notice: Three groups because there are three kinds of place to be. Getting between them is the whole cost of the master-only decision, so it is one click and not a menu.

title: Email accounts, the whole account
notice: 196 mailboxes across every workspace. What you purchased returns to you when a client leaves; an inbox somebody connected goes where they go. Settles 08 §16b.

title: Reassigning a mailbox
notice: The consequence before the act: that workspace stops sending immediately. Whether warm-up survives the move is marked open with engineering rather than promised.

title: Access, a client that only wants numbers
notice: Seven screens and four actions, per workspace. This is the Reports only preset, which the product hardcodes for one named account today because it cannot express it per workspace.

title: Access, a client that works its own replies
notice: An action cannot be granted without the screen it acts on, and the last screen cannot be switched off: Disable is the control that means stop.

title: Access, as an operator
notice: An operator holds one client and is often the most junior person in the account. Widening a client's access is not theirs to do, and the screen says so rather than rendering a dead table.

title: The same client, logged in
notice: One screen, landed on, with a plain sentence about what it cannot do. The rail and the tabs are one navigation, so there is no door into a room nobody built.

title: Templates, agency library
notice: Pattern A. Publishing puts a template in every client workspace without copying it; locking stops a client changing it. Both columns are switches, so the consequence is visible rather than argued.

title: Templates, inside a client workspace
notice: The other half. Northwind rewrote the locked opener, so it sees its own version and the agency library is untouched. Nothing here reaches another client.

section: Depth, counts that agree with their lists
title: A client's sending estate
notice: 54 mailboxes across six domains, because 41,300 sends in nine days needs them. The disconnected account at the top is the same one the Dashboard is raising.

section: Depth, counts that agree with their lists
title: The whole estate, expanded
notice: Health across the estate is the line an agency reads here, not the addresses.

section: Depth, counts that agree with their lists
title: Twelve sequences, per client
notice: Every sequence, named for this client's vertical, with figures that total the client's headline exactly. Contacted is a subset of prospects, which it was not before.

section: Depth, counts that agree with their lists
title: A first page of prospects
notice: Alloy claims 5,980 prospects and used to open on an empty table. Every row opens into a real email trail.

title: People, the whole roster
notice: One row per person. The count answers who reaches how many; the names under it are the check on that count. "Mixed" is the flag that access differs between a person's own workspaces.

title: A workspace only the owner can reach
notice: Counted and then named. Work in an uncovered workspace stops when the owner is away, and the owner is the one person whose access nobody else can grant.

title: One person, two questions
notice: Account role on the left: what they may do to the business, ticked off the same table the app enforces. Workspace access on the right: where, and to what. Sam is full on Alloy and reports-only on Northwind, and no role was invented to say so.

title: An admin across five workspaces
notice: Each preset is spelled out from the modules and verbs it actually grants, so the description cannot drift from the behaviour. The workspaces they are not in are named, because otherwise nobody can tell what is missing.

title: The two changes nobody may make
notice: You cannot demote yourself, because someone has to be able to undo a mistake and it cannot be the person who made it. The last owner cannot be demoted either. Both are disabled with the reason on screen, not hidden.

title: An invite grants a role and no workspaces
notice: They can sign in and will see nothing until added to a workspace. Owner is not offered: it is transferred, not granted, because an account with two people who can delete it has no safe state.

title: Adding someone to a workspace
notice: Access starts at whatever is picked here and is narrowed afterwards without removing them. The five sets are the same ones a client user gets, so there is nothing to learn twice.

title: One permission system, not two
notice: A client user has no role of their own: what they reach is the workspace's, set once above. Two controls over one outcome disagreed, and the invite quoted the losing one.

title: Revealing leads spends the agency's money
notice: The action that was missing from the four. Search is free, revealing is not, and the client sees whose credits it spends against a cap it did not set.

title: The invite says what they will actually meet
notice: Derived from the access set, not quoted from a role. Brightline used to be invited with "See everything of your own, including the full email trail, and reply" and met one screen.

title: The validation panel
notice: Twelve topics in the order that builds on itself, each carrying the claim it is there to test and what would change our mind. Reactions and notes export as Markdown.

title: Collapsed, during the demo
notice: Bottom-anchored so the app keeps its full width and the Dashboard keeps two columns. Escape hides it entirely.

title: T1 Settings
notice: Which workspace owns each value is the new information here; the controls themselves already exist.

title: Settings, migration roll back
notice: Available for 30 days. The modal states what rolling back costs, because the phrase sounds free and is not.

title: J1 Accept invite
notice: Outside the shell entirely. Names the agency, not Saleshandy, and says plainly that the agency never sees the password.

title: C1 Sequences, as the client
notice: The product they already know, minus the agency's administration. No switcher, no other client.

title: C2 Prospects, as the client
notice: Their own records only. Neither client can see that an overlap with another client exists.

title: C3 Usage, at a limit
notice: Every number names the agency as the one who set it, and says asking goes to them, not to Saleshandy.

title: C3, asking for more
notice: Amount and reason, both required. The agency's approve or deny is only a real decision if the client stated both.

title: C3, a linked client
notice: No allocation table, because there is no allocation. It says the agency cannot raise it and asking will not help.

title: C4 Your update
notice: The agency's voice on their own numbers. The interview says this is ad hoc, not monthly, so it is an export rather than a cycle.

title: Workspace, linked client
notice: Revoke lives here, in their account, not the agency's. The agency is told, not asked.

title: Revoking the agency
notice: Same data outcome as unlink, initiated from the other side.

title: C0 Link request
notice: In their own account, which has no agency features until one asks. Four regions: who is asking, what they get, what they do not get, what stays theirs.

title: The client's own account, no agency
notice: No Dashboard, no switcher, no Client Management, ever. The identity is theirs, not an agency staffer's.

title: After approving
notice: The agency joins as Manager, not owner, because the client owns the workspace. That asymmetry is the whole of Linked mode.

title: A0 Dashboard, as a manager
notice: Three of seven clients, and no cost column: billing visibility is a per-person toggle, not a role.

title: Where an operator lands
notice: Never the Dashboard. A half-redacted portfolio screen is worse than not offering one.

title: A3 as the owner
notice: Disable, Delete and View as client. Delete is the owner's alone.

title: A3 as a manager
notice: Disable but not Delete. A reversible pause is the manager's; ending the relationship is not.

title: Deleting a created client
notice: The agency keeps everything. Consequences per row, and a 30 day window.

title: Unlinking a linked client
notice: Nothing is deleted, because none of it is the agency's to delete. Re-linking needs their approval again.

title: Q1b From the queue to the broken mailbox
notice: The top queue item lands on the mailbox it is about, first in the list, with Reconnect on the row. Back to queue and Next in queue in the header.

title: A2b Overview with the 14-day chart
notice: Decided 12 Sep: the Overview carries the same 14-day chart the client sees on Reports, plus last activity.

title: A3b Limits edited as a draft
notice: A changed number is a draft until Apply. The bar states before and after. Inputs are formatted and carry their unit.

title: A4b Access, read only for an operator
notice: An operator reads what the account decided and cannot change it. Controls disabled in place; no denied panel.

title: A6b Domains, in the estate
notice: Decided 12 Sep: domains and Inframail IPs live in the estate, owned by the agency. Warm-up is a state on the mailbox.

title: A6c Inframail IPs
notice: Sending IPs and the purchased domains on each.

title: C7 Settings, the client's own
notice: Profile, password, notifications. Nothing of the agency's behind it. A client can change their own password again.

title: X1 Dashboard at forty
notice: The ranked table shows the eight that most need you and points at the full list. Falling needs a quarter down and at least a point down, so it flags a minority.

title: X2 Clients, 25 a page, search that works
notice: Twenty-five a page with a pager, and a search over name, company and email. The product's own page size.

title: X3 The estate at 510 mailboxes
notice: Fifty a page, a health facet, a search over address and workspace, and the source as an icon that explains itself on hover.

title: X4 The switcher at forty
notice: Six clients visible before it scrolls, search on top, and a client's limit state in words instead of a coloured dot.

title: X5 People at forty
notice: Counts are the answer, names are the check: long memberships and the uncovered tile cap at a few names and say how many more.

title: G1 The agency, five days into the grace period
notice: Decided 12 Sep: the failed payment is the first thing on the Dashboard and the first item in the queue. Clients keep reading; nothing sends.

title: G2 What the client sees during it
notice: Paused, in the agency's name, with no reason given. Everything is still readable.

title: G3 Consent card with the view-as grant
who: The client, in their own account
notice: Decided 12 Sep: on a linked workspace the agency opens it as the client only if the client switched this on. Off by default.
